title: A path stays in its SCC
prompt: Prove every vertex on a directed path between two vertices in the same strongly connected component is also in that component.

solution.text: Let u and v be in one SCC, and x lie on a directed path from u to v.
The path provides u->...->x and x->...->v. Since v and u are in one SCC, there is a path v->...->u.
Concatenate x->...->v->...->u to show x reaches u, while u reaches x.
Thus x is mutually reachable with u and belongs to the same SCC.

subject: dm
title: Bridge iff no cycle
prompt: Show an edge e in a simple undirected graph is a cut edge iff it lies on no simple circuit.

solution.text: If e lies on a simple circuit, the other circuit edges give an alternate path between its endpoints after deleting e. Every route using e can be rerouted, so deleting e does not increase the number of components. Thus e is not a cut edge.
Conversely, suppose e=uv is not a cut edge. Its endpoints remain connected in G-e. Choose a simple u-v path there.
Adding e to that path creates a simple circuit containing e.
Thus e is a cut edge exactly when it belongs to no simple circuit.

title: Mutual reachability transitive
prompt: If u,v are mutually reachable and v,w are mutually reachable in a directed graph, prove u,w are mutually reachable.

Likewise w->...->v followed by v->...->u gives a path from w to u.
Thus u reaches w and w reaches u, so they are mutually reachable.

subject: dm
title: Odd circuit forbids two colors
prompt: Show a simple graph containing a circuit with an odd number of vertices cannot be colored with two colors.

solution.text: Let the odd cycle be v1,v2,...,v_(2*k+1),v1.
In a proper two-coloring, adjacent cycle vertices must alternate colors. Thus odd-indexed vertices have the color of v1 and even-indexed vertices the other color.
Since 2*k+1 is odd, v_(2*k+1) and v1 have the same color but are adjacent. This is impossible.
Therefore the graph cannot be colored using two colors.
